title: Glacier Shelf — Frosted Conference Opener
description: A single diagonal frosted-glass slab carves across a saturated teal-to-indigo gradient, giving keynote title slides the cinematic stillness of a main-stage moment. Unlike multi-card glass layouts, there is exactly one element: the slab, the type, and the atmosphere.
philosophy: This template exists for the ten seconds before a talk begins — when the room dims and the title alone must justify why hundreds of people showed up. It refuses iconography, symmetry, and secondary UI chrome on principle; the off-axis slab creates deliberate compositional tension that signals intention without shouting. Design confidence here means trusting a gradient and a single frosted plane to carry the entire emotional weight of an opening. It is built for speakers who understand that restraint is a form of authority.
goodFor: Opening title card for a 30–60 minute conference keynote
Single-thesis reveal projected in a darkened auditorium
Speaker name / talk title introduction at large-format scale
Section breaks requiring a dramatic visual reset between talk chapters
avoidFor: Chart-heavy quarterly reviews or data-dense slide sequences
Decks requiring persistent logo lockups or sponsor branding
Bright ambient-light rooms where frosted glass contrast washes out
Multi-topic agendas needing bullet lists or structured body copy
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide feels like the moment a conference hall dims before the first word is spoken — a single luminous diagonal plane drifts across a deep, saturated atmospheric field, its frosted surface holding quiet translucency rather than shine. Composition is asymmetric and gravitationally low-center, the off-axis slab creating deliberate tension against the vast stillness of the surrounding gradient. The mood is cinematic restraint at maximum scale: one element, one gesture, one thesis. Avoid all secondary decoration, icon clusters, rule lines, grid artifacts, or any visual element that exists outside or alongside the slab.

examples.layoutNotes: Full-bleed canvas, zero outer margin — the gradient extends to all four edges with no border or breathing frame. A single frosted-glass slab enters from the lower-left edge and exits through the upper-right at a shallow diagonal, its vertical midpoint landing just below the horizontal centerline of the frame. Title and subtitle copy live entirely within the slab, constrained to a 12-col inner grid with text occupying cols 2–9 and baseline-anchored to the slab's lower interior zone. No header band, no footer bar, no page number, no decorative rule lines — absolute chrome silence outside the slab itself.

examples.promptCore: The content slide inherits the keynote's cinematic stillness — one frosted slab dominates, now angled to open more atmosphere above while anchoring a single idea below. The mood is that of a dim auditorium holding one thesis at a time: unhurried, authoritative, and spatially generous. Asymmetric breathing between the glassy content zone and the gradient void above sustains compositional tension without crowding. Avoid icons, decorative dividers, or any secondary chrome that would fracture the template's single-plane discipline.

examples.layoutNotes: Full-bleed canvas with the single frosted-glass slab repositioned to anchor lower-left through center-right, releasing the upper-right quadrant as uninterrupted gradient void. All content lives entirely within the slab's interior — one dominant statement sitting at the slab's upper rail and one subordinate line (attribution, metric, or clarifying phrase) below it, separated by weight contrast alone. Active text occupies cols 2–8 of a 12-column grid, respecting the slab's diagonal boundary so type never bleeds into raw gradient. No header band, no icon well, no footer chrome beyond an optional hairline page marker at the bottom-right edge.
